America.title: Ballot scanners failing across Westchester County polling places
America.summary: Westchester County says its Board of Elections is aware of an issue with the paper ballots that is stopping voting machines from accepting them at polling locations throughout the county. Voters are still filling out paper ballots, which poll workers are placing in secure emergency bags to be counted later. New York Attorney General Letitia James says her office is monitoring and in touch with state and local election boards, and NBC News and lohud report machines down at multiple sites, including White Plains. Al Jazeera English also reports the scanner failures and says ballots are being collected in emergency orange bags to be counted later. Rep. Lawler and others say the bags will be police-escorted to the Board of Elections after polls close at 9 p.m., New York's normal closing time. Update, unconfirmed: an unverified account posts that Westchester County Police will take about 90,000 sealed, unscanned ballots to the Board of Elections, to be unsealed tomorrow in front of watchers before counting. No official Westchester or Board of Elections post confirming that figure or timeline was found. Update: the RNC's election-integrity account says the unscanned ballots will go under police custody to the Board of Elections for central counting with watchers present, and that counting will begin no later than 11 a.m. Wednesday. That timing comes from a partisan account and hasn't been posted by the county or the Board of Elections on X. Update, midnight ET: a judge issued emergency rules for counting the unscanned ballots, Spectrum News NY1's Gloria Pazmino reports, and Examiner Media says Republicans and Democrats agreed to seek court approval for a supervised process to secure and count them. Deccan Chronicle, carrying a wire report, says the judge let officials move thousands of paper ballots to a secure county warehouse under police escort, where they will be scanned under party supervision, delaying the count in the competitive 17th Congressional District until Wednesday. News 12's Nicholas Zifcak, reporting from the Board of Elections in White Plains, says counting at the BOE facility on the Saw Mill Parkway starts Wednesday at 11 a.m., and lohud reports County Executive Ken Jenkins says the ballots will be counted. Figures of 332 sites and 250,000 ballots circulating on X come from partisan and unverified accounts and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections. lohud reports provisional paper ballots have been delivered to the Westchester Board of Elections, and The Rye Record reports the board says it will begin counting the emergency-bag ballots at 11 a.m. Wednesday. Update, 6 AM ET: ABC7NY (verified) reports the delayed Westchester ballots have been counted, with Conley and Bennett declared winners; Rep. Lawler had conceded NY-17 to Cait Conley before 11 p.m. Tuesday, per multiple posts. Figures of up to 332 sites and 250,000 ballots still trace to partisan outlets and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections.
America.status: Delayed ballots reported counted (ABC7NY); stabilizing, moving to routine coverage

Bitcoin News (verified) relays the bank saying attackers entered through a service-provider platform and used the bank's own account for fraudulent wires that could be converted to crypto; the bank says client accounts were not used and customers face no financial loss, while validating the order of magnitude of reported loss figures. Paris prosecutors are involved per earlier coverage.
Europe.status: Bank confirms ~€100M missing; contained per bank; customer accounts said unaffected; probe ongoing

Europe.title: Fire at Tbilisi building housing opposition-leaning Formula TV; staff trapped
Europe.summary: A fire broke out at the business center in Tbilisi that houses Formula TV, one of Georgia's few remaining opposition-leaning broadcasters, and the channel went off air, Civil.ge reports. Part of the staff remained inside as firefighters arrived. A Georgian journalist posted that 22 people, including opposition leader Zurab Japaridze, were to be evacuated through windows and by crane because the stairs were too dangerous. The cause of the fire has not been reported.
Europe.status: Early reports; rescue under way; cause unknown; no casualty figures

Europe.title: Second wave of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration
Europe.location: Across Europe, including Belgium, Sweden, Germany, Romania and the UK
Europe.summary: FBI Cyber Branch and FBI San Diego (verified), with CISA, HHS, USDA and DOT, issued a joint fact sheet today warning that industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems are being targeted globally across critical infrastructure, putting food and medicine inventory at risk. This follows the second wave of European supermarket refrigeration cyberattacks already logged as HIGH, plus the French EFS blood-service cold-storage intrusion via contractor Coolworld. The National (verified) covers who may be behind European blood-bank and supermarket cold-storage attacks. Organizations are urged to apply the mitigations and report suspicious activity to the FBI.
Europe.status: Official US multi-agency fact sheet issued Nov 5; ongoing global targeting of refrigeration OT; European supermarket/blood-bank incidents previously confirmed

Europe.title: Cyberattack on French blood service contractor's cold storage
Europe.summary: Le Canard enchaîné reports that on the night of Nov 1–2 hackers attacked a contractor of the Établissement français du sang (EFS), France's blood service, and heated cold rooms holding blood samples, set to stay at minus 30 degrees, up to 110 degrees. FrenchBreaches names the contractor as Coolworld and says the incident was detected in time with no reported operational impact. It resembles the refrigeration attacks on European supermarkets. Update, 8 PM ET Nov 4: ABC News reports no blood products were compromised. Update, midnight ET Nov 5: GB News reports hackers targeted French blood banks in the latest European refrigeration cyberattack, and ABC7 News Bay Area likewise reports the blood-bank site was hit but no blood products were compromised. Attribution remains unknown.
Europe.status: Multiple outlets; no blood products compromised per ABC/ABC7; no EFS statement found on X this sweep; attribution unknown

Europe.title: Moldova suspects a state actor behind cyberattack
Europe.summary: Moldova's prime minister told Euronews the government suspects a state actor is behind a cyberattack. The Euronews post does not detail which systems were hit; unverified posts claim government databases and citizens' ID data were compromised.
Europe.status: Official statement reported by Euronews; scope and attribution under investigation

Europe.title: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 European flights; fighter escorts and diversions
Europe.location: Europe-wide (Ireland, France, Italy, Austria, Czechia, Bulgaria, Poland, Spain and other routes)
Europe.summary: Reuters (verified) reports a second wave this week of hoax bomb threats hitting European airlines from Ireland to Bulgaria, with at least 25 flights making unplanned landings or receiving fighter escorts in its earlier tally; multiple secondary accounts citing Reuters now put Thursday's total at least at 27, including a KLM Amsterdam–Tel Aviv flight diverted for inspection in Bucharest. An Aer Lingus Dublin–Rome flight was diverted to a French military base. No explosives have been reported found. Ynet Global and economist Steve Hanke also cover the wave.
Europe.status: Ongoing hoax wave; no confirmed explosives; scale at least mid-20s per Reuters and secondary tallies

Europe.title: Violent cost-of-living and anti-government protests
Europe.summary: On Oct 31, masked rioters looted shops in Frankfurt, and German police fired water cannons at youths throwing Molotov cocktails. In Paris and elsewhere in France, police fired tear gas as hundreds of thousands marched against living costs and police violence. In Tirana, protesters threw Molotov cocktails and paving stones at police. Swiss paper Tages-Anzeiger says the riots also reached Switzerland over the weekend, with protests in Zurich. On Tuesday, French students marched through central Paris despite the authorities rejecting their route, Reuters reports, and DW says German officials are looking for those responsible for the Gen Z protest riots.
Europe.status: Confirmed by major outlets; further marches possible

Europe.title: Spyware alerts for German officials
Europe.summary: People who received the alerts were told to treat their phones as compromised. It is not yet known who is behind the attack or how many people were affected.

Europe.title: Poland deploys counterterrorism police near Kaliningrad
Europe.summary: Poland has deployed police counterterrorism units near the Kaliningrad border after intelligence warnings of possible sabotage in the coming days, the Kyiv Independent reports, citing Polish media.

Europe.title: Latvia says drones violated its airspace
Europe.summary: Latvia believes one of two drones that violated its airspace was Russian and the other Ukrainian, Reuters reports.

Europe.title: Germany arrests suspected organizer of Starlink ground station arson in Poland
Europe.location: Reutlingen district, Germany / Wola Krobowska, Poland
Europe.summary: German special police arrested a Turkish national on Nov 3 suspected of ordering the Sept 23 arson attack on a Starlink ground station south of Warsaw, according to a report citing Stuttgart prosecutors. Two alleged perpetrators were arrested in October. Polish prosecutors suspect Russian intelligence involvement, which German authorities have not confirmed.

Europe.title: Student protest in Paris defies ban; tear gas near the Panthéon
Europe.summary: teleSUR English reports hundreds of students defied a protest ban in Paris to demand more education funding and economic reforms, and police used tear gas during clashes near the Panthéon. More protests are planned for November 5.
Europe.status: Early reports; single outlet; no police or official figures found

Russia.title: Major evening blackout across Kyiv after Russian strikes on energy grid
Russia.summary: Large parts of Kyiv remain dark after repeated Russian strikes on energy infrastructure, with emergency cuts and long scheduled outages. Anton Gerashchenko reports a large part of the capital in blackout Thursday evening, with many residents also lacking water or heating. Secondary posts cite Ukrenergo/DTEK emergency cuts in parts of Sviatoshynskyi, Shevchenkivskyi and Podilskyi districts; total city-wide blackout claims appear overstated relative to district-level emergency cuts. Zelenskyy has separately described nationwide plant damage.
Russia.status: Ongoing; evening blackout and water/heating hardship widely reported; district-level emergency cuts confirmed by Ukrainian voices

Russia.title: Beget, a major Russian web host, still largely offline after cloud-wiping cyberattack
Russia.summary: Beget, one of Russia's largest hosting providers (~540,000 .ru domains), reported a massive cyberattack beginning about 02:40 Moscow time on November 2 that wiped cloud servers and some backups. Network observers say on day four only a small share of the network is answering. Government and commercial clients are among those affected; full restoration timeline unclear.
Russia.status: Ongoing outage day 4+; company attributes wipe to cyberattack

Russia.title: Main gas pipeline explosion and fire in Topkinsky district, Kemerovo
Russia.location: Topki / Topkinsky district, Kemerovo Oblast, Russia (Siberia)
Russia.summary: On Nov. 5 a main gas transmission pipeline in the Topkinsky municipal district suffered depressurization, followed by a powerful explosion and large fire. Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk confirmed the fire; later reports say the blaze was extinguished. Multiple accounts note this is the second major Russian trunk-pipeline fire in about a month (after a Penza-region incident around Oct. 13). Cause remains unclear; sabotage is speculated in some posts but not proven.
Russia.status: Confirmed by regional governor; fire reported extinguished; cause under investigation / unclear

Russia.title: Water outages across all Kyiv districts after emergency power cuts at the city water utility
Russia.summary: Kyivvodokanal facilities lost power again under emergency blackouts on November 5, disrupting water across all districts; Sota News says service is gradually being restored. Afternoon videos from Saint Javelin and Military Summary show a large-scale blackout across Kyiv, with some areas getting only a few hours of power and scheduled outage calendars failing. Zelenskyy said every Ukrainian power plant has been affected and appealed for transformers, cables and generators.
Russia.status: Ongoing; water gradually restoring; citywide blackout videos afternoon of Nov 5

Russia.title: Emergency power cuts in Kyiv and four oblasts after overnight strikes on energy sites
Russia.location: Kyiv city; Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Chernihiv and Cherkasy oblasts; Sumy oblast, Ukraine
Russia.summary: OSINT account AMK Mapping says emergency power outages were imposed across Kyiv Oblast after overnight Russian jet-drone strikes on energy infrastructure, naming the Kyivska 750 kV substation and the Trypillia thermal power plant among the targets, with further emergency cuts in Zhytomyr, Chernihiv and Cherkasy oblasts and Kyiv city on top of rolling blackouts. Ukrainian outlet Blyskavka reports emergency shutdowns in parts of three Kyiv districts, across all of Sumy oblast, and in one Chernihiv district after a night attack on an energy facility. Accounts relaying Ukrenergo say scheduled outage timetables are not in force.

Russia.title: Evening drone attack on Kyiv; explosions and air defense active
Russia.summary: An air raid siren sounded in Kyiv on Wednesday evening local time, and EuromaidanPR reported explosions in the city at about 3:24 PM ET and said air defense was active over Kyiv at about 3:53 PM ET. Casualty and damage figures had not been reported by officials on X at sweep time.
Russia.status: Early reports; attack ongoing at sweep time; no official damage or casualty figures

Russia.title: Kyiv Independent hit by suspected Russian cyberattack
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent says it was hit by a suspected Russian cyberattack. Editor-in-chief Olga Rudenko said it is the first attack of this kind on the outlet and that it is being treated very seriously. The nature of the attack and any impact on the outlet's services were not described in the post.
Russia.status: Confirmed by the targeted outlet; attribution is suspected, not confirmed

Russia.title: Russian drone strike sets Odesa's 7th Kilometer market on fire
Russia.summary: Russian drones struck the 7th Kilometer market near Odesa, one of Ukraine's largest wholesale markets, on Wednesday morning, starting a large fire seen on video. One account says the strike came during the working day while the market was busy. No official casualty figures were found in the posts reviewed.
Russia.status: Early reports with video; casualties unknown

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike sets Ozon logistics hub in Adygeysk on fire
Russia.summary: A drone attack overnight on November 4 set fire to online retailer Ozon's logistics centre in Adygeysk, damaging the building and partially collapsing its roof, Militarnyi reports. Ozon confirmed the attack and said staff were evacuated, with no casualties reported, and the head of Adygea also confirmed it. Videos posted by OSINT accounts show a large fire at the site.
Russia.status: Confirmed by the company and regional head, per reports; now also reported by Reuters; damage still being assessed

Russia.title: 310-drone overnight attack on Ukraine; Zhytomyr largely without power
Russia.location: Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Odesa and other regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Russia launched 310 drones overnight into November 4, according to Ukraine's Air Force as cited by journalist Michael Bociurkiw, targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Poltava, Odesa, Ternopil and the Rivne and Kirovohrad regions. Hromadske Radio reports Zhytomyr remains largely without power after a strike, with electric transport suspended and water facilities on generators. Kyiv Post shows Kyiv in a blackout on generators, and Bociurkiw reports large parts of Odesa without power and Kyiv water only partly restored. Update, 8 PM ET: PBS News, citing Ukraine's air force, says most of the 300-plus drones were shot down but one strike set a shopping center ablaze in western Ukraine, injuring at least one person.

Russia.title: Russian bombing kills 43 at aid point in Komyshuvakha; dozens still missing
Russia.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the death toll from a Russian strike on an aid point in Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia region) has risen to 43, with Anadolu Agency and other outlets confirming the figure. Zelenskyy also said the toll could climb toward 100 as rescue work continues and dozens remain missing. The strike hit people who had gathered for aid including bread.
Russia.status: Confirmed 43 dead per Zelenskyy; rescue ongoing; possible higher toll

Russia.title: Massive overnight Russian strike on Ukraine's power grid
Russia.location: Odesa, Cherkasy, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Chernivtsi, Chernihiv and Rivne regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Mass Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy system on Nov. 3 triggered Kyiv's most severe water outage of the full-scale invasion, the Kyiv Independent reported citing three people with knowledge of the matter including a government advisor; Rob Lee amplified the report overnight. Residents across most Kyiv districts went more than 24 hours without water after power to pumping was cut. AMK Mapping separately logged continued large-scale Geran drone and cruise-missile attacks overnight (200+ drones), with targets including substations and power plants around Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Dnipro and elsewhere.
Russia.status: Confirmed water outage cascading from Nov. 3 grid strikes; drone campaign continuing

Russia.title: New overnight Russian drone attack; eastern Kyiv power loss reported
Russia.summary: NOELreports, citing Ukraine's Air Force, says Russia launched 310 drones overnight into Nov. 4, including 81 jet-powered Shaheds, with 272 downed or suppressed and strikes recorded at 19 locations. OSINT account AMK Mapping says almost all of eastern Kyiv lost power overnight after jet-drone strikes on energy infrastructure, including the Kyivska 750 kV substation. Russia.title: Emergency alert apps in Ukraine and Russia hacked
Russia.summary: Ukraine and Russia both said their emergency alert apps had been hacked, sending false warnings about air raids and chemical and nuclear attacks. Russia said its app suffered a "massive cyberattack" on Monday, hours after Ukraine reported its own hack. In Ukraine the fake nuclear warning caused unease but not panic. Zelenskyy told PBS NewsHour that Ukraine targeted Russia's emergency alert systems in a retaliatory hack. Hackmanac reports the attacker exploited a flaw in the admin panel of the Russian Emergency Ministry app to push false alerts across 33 regions.
Russia.status: Officially confirmed by both governments; Zelenskyy says Ukraine's hack of Russian alerts was retaliation

Russia.title: Drone strike kills two at Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant says a Ukrainian drone killed two people, including a station employee, Reuters reports. Ukraine's response and any IAEA comment weren't seen in this sweep.
Russia.status: Claim by the Russian-installed plant management, reported by Reuters; not independently confirmed

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike reported on Yaroslavl oil refinery
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports that Ukraine struck the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl with drones overnight on Nov. 3, with residents reporting several fires at the facility, citing Ukrainian monitoring channels. OSINT accounts posted video of fires in the industrial zone, and the independent Russian outlet ASTRA reported explosions in the area. Russian officials had not confirmed damage or casualties at the time of this sweep. Kyiv Post reports the Slavneft-owned refinery caught fire after the drone attack.
Russia.status: Early reports; no official Russian statement yet

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike reported on Samara oil facility
Russia.summary: Ukrainian monitoring channels reported that Ukrainian drones struck the Samara Linear Production and Dispatch Station in Prosvet overnight. Kazakhstan reportedly suspended oil pumping through the Atyrau-Samara pipeline after the attack on the Samara hub, with its Energy Ministry cited via TASS.
Russia.status: Strike reported by Ukrainian channels; Kazakh halt reported via TASS and market wires, not yet seen from major Western outlets

Russia.title: Large Ukrainian drone raid toward western Russia under way tonight
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a Ukrainian attack drone raid into western Russia is under way tonight, with local channels reporting jet-powered drones in the mix and several hundred drones headed toward Russian targets. It follows five straight nights of hits on Russian oil installations. Separately, Eyewitness News reports Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said Tuesday that air defenses downed nearly 500 drones headed toward the capital; it isn't clear whether that figure covers tonight's raid.

Russia.title: Widespread blackout across Russian-occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Accounts on both sides report a widespread power outage across Crimea on Nov. 3–4, with video of Simferopol in darkness. ConflictRadarME quotes Oleg Kryuchkov, an adviser to the Russian-installed Crimean head, saying an incident on external grid infrastructure cut the main supply. A pro-Russian WarGonzo account reports rolling cuts, water pumping problems and emergency mobile roaming, and Beefeater, citing Crimea.Realities, reports fuel shortages. The cause is not established.

Russia.title: Kyiv residents block road over day-long power outage
Russia.summary: An unverified account posts video it says shows residents of Kyiv's Obolon district blocking a road to protest a power outage lasting nearly a full day, and says similar pickets are being organized elsewhere in the city. It follows the large Russian strike on Ukraine's grid.
Russia.status: Single unverified source; no official or major-outlet confirmation found on X

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike sets Ryazan oil refinery on fire
Russia.summary: Overnight Nov 4–5, Ukrainian drones hit the Rosneft Ryazan oil refinery (~340,000 b/d, ~5% of Russian refining; supplies Moscow fuels including military). Governor Pavel Malkov reported 200+ drones in the region; fires at industrial sites were reported contained. Middle East.title: Stabbing attack in Amman kills a police officer; Jordan calls it terrorism

Al Jazeera English and other outlets report the suspect was arrested. No motive or affiliation has been released.

Middle East.title: Tanker struck by two unidentified projectiles north of Qatar
Middle East.location: Persian Gulf, about 50 nautical miles north of Qatar
Middle East.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) reported that a tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles north of Qatar late Wednesday. The condition of the crew and the extent of damage were not known in the reports. It extends this week's attacks on shipping beyond the Strait of Hormuz.
Middle East.status: UKMTO report relayed by several outlets; crew and damage unknown; attacker not identified

Middle East.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired toward Medina
Middle East.summary: The Saudi-led coalition's spokesperson, Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Malki, said air defenses intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched toward the Madinah region on Thursday, as reported by Saudi Gazette, Khaleej Times and Kuwait Times. No damage or casualties were reported in the posts reviewed. It follows the Houthis' claimed missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, logged earlier.
Middle East.status: Official coalition statement issued; no damage reported

Middle East.title: Israel says it foiled a bomb-and-shooting plot at Jerusalem's Lions' Gate
Middle East.summary: Accounts citing the Shin Bet and Israeli police report that a 19-year-old East Jerusalem resident was arrested over a plan to detonate an explosive at Lions' Gate and then open fire on civilians and officers at the Temple Mount. The reports say he confessed and that an indictment has been filed. No attack took place.

Middle East.title: Houthis claim ballistic missile strike on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport
Middle East.summary: Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed the group struck King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh with a ballistic missile, causing significant damage. The Houthis also called on international airlines to avoid Saudi airspace. Saudi authorities had not confirmed any details in the posts reviewed, and no independent damage reports were found.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed Houthi claim; no Saudi statement found on X

Middle East.title: Reported security incident at the Israeli President's office
Middle East.summary: CGTN Africa posted a one-line report of a security incident at the office of Israel's president. No details, casualties or official statement were found, and searches found no other source on X yet.
Middle East.status: Early, single-source report

Middle East.title: Houthi missile strike on Lahj health center kills five
Middle East.summary: A ballistic missile attributed to the Houthis hit the Al-Saqiya health center in Lahj, killing five people and injuring 15, including medical staff, according to Yemen's government-aligned forces and local outlets. UNICEF, which supports the center, said the attack was deeply concerning, and the British ambassador to Yemen condemned it. Separately, South24 cites a military source saying a Houthi missile hit a detention site in Lahj early Wednesday, killing two.
Middle East.status: Casualty toll from Yemeni government side; UN agency and UK ambassador statements reported; second strike single-source

Middle East.title: IRGC claims it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper over the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone over the Strait of Hormuz early Wednesday and released video they say shows the hit. The claim is circulating through OSINT and aggregator accounts. No US military confirmation was found on X this sweep.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed IRGC claim; no CENTCOM statement found

Middle East.title: Missile strike on recruit training camp in Yemen's Al Dhale
Middle East.location: Al-Alalah camp, Qa'tabah district, Al Dhale, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Yemeni outlets report a ballistic missile strike attributed to the Houthis hit the Al-Alalah training camp for new recruits in Qa'tabah district on Wednesday morning. Update: The New Arab now reports more than 25 recruits killed and dozens wounded. Earlier tolls ranged from 11 to 20 killed (South24, YemenOnline, Al Bawaba), and there is still no official government figure on X.

Middle East.title: US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
Middle East.location: Qeshm Island, Strait of Hormuz, Iran
Middle East.summary: A US official told Reuters that the US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Monday, Nov. 2. The Economic Times, citing The Wall Street Journal, says it is the latest in a series of limited, unpublicized US strikes in recent weeks. Iran's state news agency IRNA earlier reported five explosions on the island. Officials quoted in media describe the strike as a defensive response to Iranian surface-to-air fire on a US aircraft; CENTCOM has not issued a statement. An Israeli military spokesperson says Israel was not involved. On Nov 3, President Trump said the US carried out a "minor attack" in Iran overnight, claiming Iranian ships and planes were destroyed and insisting it was not a war, per Al Jazeera. Iran's security chief said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only if the US met Iran's seven conditions. Later on Nov 3, Reuters, citing a Financial Times interview, reported Trump said the US has no immediate plan to strike Iran again.
Middle East.status: US strikes acknowledged by President Trump; damage and casualty claims not independently confirmed; no CENTCOM statement found

Middle East.summary: India's shipping minister says the Indian vessel MSV AL JUSUFI, carrying 14 Indian seafarers, was struck by an unidentified aerial object near the Omani coast on Nov. 2. Middle East.summary: Reuters reports Syria says it foiled a Hezbollah plot to attack the Homs oil refinery. No attack took place.

Middle East.title: Unconfirmed report of explosion at British Embassy in Baghdad
Middle East.summary: Iran's Tasnim News Agency reported explosions heard inside the British Embassy in Baghdad. Other accounts describe a roadside device hitting a diplomatic vehicle instead. No official confirmation, casualties or damage details have been seen.

Middle East.title: Houthis claim drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's Dammam airport
Middle East.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed drone attacks over the past 48 hours on Dammam airport, which he said disrupted air traffic, and on military targets in Jizan. Middle East.title: Unexplained explosion in Iraq's Diyala province
Middle East.summary: Faytuks Network reports an explosion on the outskirts of Diyala that was reportedly heard in neighboring Salah al-Din, with locals describing intense military aircraft activity. Security officials told Iraqi Sabereen News the cause and nature of the blast are unknown.

Middle East.title: Israeli air strike kills police officers near Khan Younis
Middle East.summary: Gaza's interior ministry says an Israeli air strike killed and wounded several police officers near Khan Younis. The number of casualties wasn't given.

Middle East.title: Drones strike Iranian Kurdish group Komala's HQ near Erbil
Middle East.location: Alana Valley, northeast of Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan

Earlier removals: the DC Foggy Bottom outage, the Richmond pump station outage, the San Diego registrar evacuation (cleared), the Mississauga police incident, the Hebron operation, the Florida Learjet crash, and the Fairfield and Moss Landing shootings. A seven-minute pause for a school safety drill at a Gwinnett County, GA polling place, with a requested seven-minute extension, was below the bar. The Oct. 28 Urda, Spain high-speed train collision is past the acute phase; Spain's transport minister said Tuesday he will resign over it (Reuters).

threats.title: Viral 'another Maricopa vote center closed' claim is unsourced
threats.summary: Posts claim a second, 'Republican-leaning' Maricopa County vote center in Mesa closed for a power outage, some calling for the election to be stopped. Maricopa County Elections' own posts show only the Laveen Elementary School District Office closure for a power outage early Tuesday, and no official source confirms a second closure.

threats.title: Low-priority log
threats.summary: Fraud and 'rigged' framing of the Westchester scanner failure, the Fulton County rescan and the Maricopa Laveen outage has no official support. Unverified posts claim the refrigeration attacks spread to 13 European countries and to US military installations. A 'Worldwide Alert' roundup from the Paul Gold Eagle account mixes real events with unsupported claims. A Florida 'state beach shooting' post from a low-credibility account appears to confuse the Moss Landing, California shooting and has no corroboration. Claims of an official 90-day blackout warning have no official source. Earlier unsupported claims (Jacksonville blackout, a successful Iranian strike on a US base in Kuwait, Russia hitting six power plants) still have no corroboration. Posts claiming widespread Pennsylvania scanner failures got a reply from the Pennsylvania Department of State saying scanner jams don't stop ballots from being counted and that it has no reports of widespread scanner issues. Viral 'Iran nuclear survival guide' and 'massive Iran internet blackout' posts come from low-credibility accounts; see the sourced internet-outage item instead. 7:30 PM sweep: viral video of multi-hour lines in Columbus, OH is circulating as Election Day footage, but replies identify it as past early-voting footage from the Franklin County Board of Elections site, so it was not logged. Unverified claims that Newaygo County, MI ran out of ballots and that Wayne County polls lost power just before closing found no official or verified-outlet support. Partisan 'cheating' framing around the Gibraltar threat was ignored. 8 PM sweep: a viral post claiming Wayne County polling places lost power remains unsupported beyond the single Canton Township report logged above; claims of a Mesa, AZ vote-center power closure 'per the Recorder's Office' still have no official source. New this sweep: a small account claims a 'BulkaHackers' arrest in Kosovo with no corroboration; posts framing Wayne County results as delayed countywide by fraud have no official support; posts claiming an Iranian missile barrage on Israel are contradicted in replies and by the lack of any official or major-outlet report; and PaulGoldEagle-style posts claiming more Ohio threats remain unsupported. New tonight: an unverified viral post claims a San Diego library ballot drop box overflowed and ballots were mishandled; the San Diego County Registrar has not addressed it on X, and it is not confirmed. A King County, WA 'voter fraud' video claim comes from a low-credibility account with no official support. Claims of a 'major power outage' on Colorado's Front Range are contradictory and have no utility or official source. Claims that Iran launched a massive hypersonic missile attack on Israeli bases come from low-credibility accounts and are not reported by the IDF or major outlets. 2:00 AM sweep: a new Paul Gold Eagle roundup lists Election Day voting disruptions across several states and frames them as deliberate interference without official confirmation; it is not logged as an alert. 4 PM sweep: a viral thread claiming hackers are hitting 'the world's money system in 7 places at once' was checked by another account, which found the incidents are separate, mostly already known, and include an ECB malware story it could only trace to 2019; it is not one coordinated attack. A post predicting a nationwide blackout this month has no source. Claims that the Paraguay banking crisis caused riots beyond the Asunción clashes logged above come from low-credibility accounts, and a Paraguay-based account calls a viral 'riots in Paraguay' video clickbait. 8 PM sweep: recurring posts claiming Election Day power outages were used to slip in fake ballots have no official or verified-outlet source and are not logged. 10 PM sweep: posts claiming a new White House shooting today recycle the May 23, 2026 checkpoint shooting, per a fact-check reply, and are not logged. A post claiming Netanyahu was seriously injured in an attack in Tel Aviv comes from a GESARA-branded account with no corroboration. Crypto-account framing of the Crédit Mutuel Arkéa breach as part of a coordinated attack on the global financial system remains unsupported.
